q: How tall is One World Trade Center in New York, including its spire?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: Its height in feet, 1,776, matches the year of the US Declaration of Independence.

q: How tall is the Atomium in Brussels?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It shows a single iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

q: How tall is the London Eye?
hint: For scale: Big Ben’s Elizabeth Tower is {96 m} tall.
card: A full turn takes about 30 minutes, slow enough that people step on and off while it keeps moving.

q: How wide is the dome of the Pantheon in Rome?
hint: For scale: a basketball court is about {28 m} long.
card: Nearly 1,900 years on, it is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

q: How tall is Chicago’s Willis Tower, to its roof?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall with its antennas.
card: It was called the Sears Tower until 2009.

q: How tall is each letter of the Hollywood sign?
hint: For scale: a giraffe stands about {5.5 m} tall.
card: It first read “HOLLYWOODLAND” and was put up in 1923 to advertise a housing development.

q: In what year did London’s Tower Bridge open?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889.
card: Its high walkways between the towers were closed in 1910 because so few people used them.

q: How tall is the Great Sphinx of Giza?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It was carved from the limestone bedrock of the Giza Plateau.

q: In what year did the Channel Tunnel open?
hint: For scale: the Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
card: Its tunnels reach up to 75 m below sea level.

q: How tall is the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab hotel in Dubai?
hint: For scale: a 30-storey office tower is about {100 m} tall.
card: It stands on its own artificial island about 280 m offshore.

q: How many rooms are in Buckingham Palace?
hint: For scale: a typical family house has about six to eight rooms.
card: Queen Victoria was the first monarch to live there, from 1837.

q: How long is Hadrian’s Wall in northern England?
hint: For scale: a marathon is just over {42 km}.
card: Roman soldiers built most of it in about six years, starting around AD 122.

q: In what year was the first image of a black hole revealed?
hint: For scale: gravitational waves were first detected in 2015.
card: It showed the black hole at the centre of the galaxy M87, about 53 million light-years away.

q: Roughly how hot is the core of the Sun?
hint: For scale: the Sun’s visible surface is about {5,500 °C}.
card: Light made there can take over 100,000 years to work its way out to the surface.

q: How old is the universe?
hint: For scale: the oldest known fossils are about 3.5 billion years old.
card: Its oldest light, the afterglow of the Big Bang, was released about 380,000 years after it began.

q: How old is the Earth?
hint: For scale: the dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago.
card: The oldest known minerals on Earth, tiny zircon crystals from Australia, are about 4.4 billion years old.

q: In what year did someone first walk in space?
hint: For scale: Yuri Gagarin first flew to space in 1961.
card: Alexei Leonov’s suit ballooned so much he had to let air out to squeeze back into his spacecraft.

q: How fast does Earth travel around the Sun?
hint: For scale: a rifle bullet flies at about {1 km/s}.
card: That’s fast enough to cross the width of the United States in under three minutes.

q: How many Moons would it take to match the mass of the Earth?
hint: For scale: about 49 Moons would fit inside Earth by volume.
card: Even so, it is the fifth-largest moon in the Solar System.

q: What percentage of Earth’s gravity would you feel on the Moon?
hint: For scale: on Mars you’d feel about 38%.
card: That’s why Apollo astronauts often found it easier to hop than to walk.

q: How many constellations are officially recognised by astronomers?
hint: For scale: the zodiac has 12 constellations.
card: The largest, Hydra, sprawls across more than 3% of the whole sky.

q: In what year was Pluto discovered?
hint: For scale: Neptune was found in 1846.
card: Its name was suggested by Venetia Burney, an 11-year-old girl in Oxford.

q: How many Earth days pass between one sunrise and the next on the Moon?
hint: For scale: the Moon takes about a week to go from new to half full.
card: So a single stretch of daylight on the Moon lasts about two Earth weeks.

q: How high is the Kármán line, the most common definition of where space begins?
hint: For scale: airliners cruise about {11 km} up.
card: It is named after Theodore von Kármán, who worked out roughly where wings stop working. So is this game.

q: How many species of bear are alive today?
hint: For scale: there are seven species of sea turtle.
card: The polar bear is the largest; the sun bear of Southeast Asia is the smallest.

q: How many bones are in one human foot?
hint: For scale: the whole adult skeleton has 206.
card: Together, your two feet hold about a quarter of all the bones in your body.

q: How fast can a greyhound run?
hint: For scale: a typical town speed limit is {50 km/h}.
card: It is widely considered the fastest dog breed, with a deep chest that holds a big heart.

q: In what year did Alexander Fleming discover penicillin?
hint: For scale: the First World War ended in 1918.
card: He noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish he had left out while on holiday.

q: In what year was the double-helix structure of DNA published?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: Rosalind Franklin’s X-ray image, “Photo 51”, was key evidence for the double helix.

q: In what year did Edward Jenner test the first vaccine, against smallpox?
hint: For scale: the US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
card: The word vaccine comes from vacca, Latin for cow, because he used cowpox.

q: How tall was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person ever reliably measured?
hint: For scale: a typical interior door is about {2 m} tall.
card: He was still growing when he died at the age of 22.

q: How many legs does a scorpion have?
hint: For scale: insects have six.
card: Scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light.

q: How many identical babies does a nine-banded armadillo usually have in one litter?
hint: For scale: humans usually have one baby at a time.
card: All of them grow from a single fertilised egg, which is why they are identical.

q: How long can a Komodo dragon grow?
hint: For scale: a typical car is about {4.5 m} long.
card: It is the largest living lizard, and can eat up to 80% of its body weight in one meal.

q: How many toes does a typical cat have, counting all four paws?
hint: For scale: a human has 20 fingers and toes.
card: Cats with extra toes are called polydactyl; Ernest Hemingway’s house in Florida is full of them.

q: How many days does a dog’s pregnancy usually last?
hint: For scale: a human pregnancy lasts about 280 days.
card: Puppies are born with their eyes closed and open them at around ten days old.

q: In what year did the Beatles release their first single, “Love Me Do”?
hint: For scale: Elvis Presley’s first big hit, “Heartbreak Hotel”, came out in 1956.
card: A session drummer, not Ringo Starr, played on one of the released versions.

q: In what year did Disneyland open in California?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: It was built in about a year on former orange groves in Anaheim.

q: In what year was gold found at Sutter’s Mill, starting the California Gold Rush?
hint: For scale: the Battle of Waterloo was fought in 1815.
card: San Francisco grew from about 1,000 people to around 25,000 in under two years.

q: In what year was the first Super Bowl played?
hint: For scale: the Beatles split up in 1970.
card: Officially it wasn’t the Super Bowl: it was the AFL-NFL World Championship Game.

q: In what year was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born?
hint: For scale: Johann Sebastian Bach died in 1750.
card: He was composing his first short pieces at the age of five.

q: In what year was the first Tour de France raced?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889.
card: It was dreamed up to boost sales of a sports newspaper, L’Auto.

q: In what year was the Mona Lisa stolen from the Louvre?
hint: For scale: Paris opened its first Métro line in 1900.
card: It was missing for over two years, and the theft is a big part of why it is so famous today.

q: In what year were the first Academy Awards handed out?
hint: For scale: the first feature-length “talkie”, The Jazz Singer, came out in 1927.
card: The ceremony lasted about 15 minutes, and the winners had been announced months before.

q: How many days did the Mayflower’s voyage across the Atlantic take?
hint: For scale: a modern cruise ship crosses in about a week.
card: One baby, Oceanus Hopkins, was born on board during the crossing.

q: Roughly how many soldiers are in China’s Terracotta Army?
hint: For scale: a Roman legion had about 5,000 soldiers.
card: Each figure has its own face, and they were originally painted in bright colours.

q: For how many years did Louis XIV reign as king of France?
hint: For scale: most US presidents serve four or eight years.
card: He became king at the age of four, so his mother and ministers ruled for him at first.

q: How many children did Queen Victoria have?
hint: For scale: Henry VIII had six wives.
card: Her children married into so many royal families that she was called “the grandmother of Europe”.

q: In what year did Apple release the first Macintosh?
hint: For scale: IBM’s first PC came out in 1981.
card: It was launched with a famous TV ad inspired by George Orwell’s novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

q: In what year was the first text message sent?
hint: For scale: the first call from a handheld mobile phone was made in 1973.
card: It said “Merry Christmas” and was typed on a computer, because phones couldn’t send texts yet.

q: What was the top speed of Japan’s first bullet trains when they opened in 1964?
hint: For scale: a car on a motorway goes about {110 km/h}.
card: The line opened just days before the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

q: In what year was the QR code invented?
hint: For scale: the first barcode was scanned at a shop checkout in 1974.
card: It was designed by the Japanese firm Denso Wave to track car parts.

q: What speed did Thrust SSC reach in 1997, the first car to officially break the sound barrier?
hint: For scale: a Formula One car tops out at around {350 km/h}.
card: It was powered by two jet engines from a Phantom fighter plane.

q: How long is a Nimitz-class aircraft carrier?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: Its nuclear reactors let it sail for over 20 years without refuelling.

q: How much did the Hubble Space Telescope weigh at launch?
hint: For scale: an adult African elephant weighs about {6,000 kg}.
card: It is about 13 m long, roughly the length of a big city bus.

q: In what year did the first music CDs go on sale?
hint: For scale: Pac-Man hit arcades in 1980.
card: The first album to go on sale was Billy Joel’s 52nd Street.

q: How many megabytes does a standard 3.5-inch high-density floppy disk hold?
hint: For scale: a typical phone photo is about 3 MB.
card: The “save” icon in many apps is still a picture of one.

q: How many revolutions per minute does a vinyl LP record spin at?
hint: For scale: a car engine idles at about 800 rpm.
card: LP stands for “long play”: about 23 minutes of music per side.

q: How tall was the very first Ferris wheel, built in Chicago in 1893?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Each of its 36 cars could hold 60 people.

q: What top speed did Usain Bolt hit during his 2009 world-record 100 m?
hint: For scale: a brisk walk is about {5 km/h}.
card: He covered the 100 m in 9.58 seconds.

q: How high is the top platform in Olympic diving?
hint: For scale: a typical room is about {2.5 m} tall.
card: Divers have under two seconds in the air to fit in all their twists and somersaults.

q: How long is an American football field between the two goal lines?
hint: For scale: a soccer pitch is usually about {105 m} long.
card: Its painted yard lines give it the nickname “the gridiron”.

q: How far is it from the foul line to the head pin in ten-pin bowling?
hint: For scale: a double-decker bus is about {11 m} long.
card: A perfect game scores 300: twelve strikes in a row.

q: How many letters are in the Hawaiian alphabet, counting the ʻokina?
hint: For scale: English has 26.
card: They are A, E, I, O, U, H, K, L, M, N, P, W and the ʻokina, a glottal stop.

q: How long is the longer side of a sheet of A4 paper?
hint: For scale: a credit card is about 86 mm wide.
card: Fold it in half and you get A5, with exactly the same proportions.

q: How many sheets are in a standard ream of paper?
hint: For scale: a typical paperback novel has about 300 pages.
card: The word comes, via Spanish, from the Arabic rizma, meaning a bundle.

q: How many seconds does an NBA team get to take a shot?
hint: For scale: a minute has 60 seconds.
card: It arrived in 1954 to stop teams stalling; one game in 1950 had ended 19–18.

q: How many tiles are in a standard double-six set of dominoes?
hint: For scale: a deck of cards has 52.
card: Every possible pairing of 0 to 6 pips appears exactly once.

q: How heavy is a standard gold bar of the kind held by central banks?
hint: For scale: a bowling ball weighs about {7 kg}.
card: Each bar must be at least 99.5% pure gold.

q: How many squares are on a Scrabble board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64.
card: Only 8 of them are triple-word squares.
